images.title: Where rainbows fall
images.caption: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hawaii
images.desc: Water, sunlight and lush greenery come together at Rainbow Falls in Hilo, on Hawaii's Big Island. Here, the Wailuku River plunges 24 metres over a lava ledge, sending mist into the air as it reaches the pool below. On sunny mornings, that mist can catch the light and produce the colourful rainbows that gave the falls their name. Known in Hawaiian as Waiānuenue, meaning 'rainbow water', this striking waterfall is surrounded by tropical vegetation and has a special place in Hawaiian legend.

images.title: When snow meets red rock
images.caption: Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA
images.desc: Snow transforms Bryce Canyon National Park, blanketing the landscape in white while its fiery orange-red hoodoos rise above the snowy terrain. Seen from Sunset Point, one of the park's most famous overlooks, these fantastical shapes are part of the Claron Formation, whose limestone was deposited about 50 million years ago and later shaped by weathering and erosion. Because much of the park rises above 2,400 metres, snow can arrive as early as October. In today's image, snow clings to the canyon's ridges and spires while mist drifts across the cliffs, creating an iconic winter scene in the American Southwest.

images.title: Autumnal camouflage
images.caption: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Scotland
images.desc: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and newer conifer woodlands, with plentiful habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts and other tasty morsels year-round. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.

images.title: Geometry in nature
images.caption: Fibonacci Day
images.desc: Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In maths, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Today is Fibonacci Day, chosen for the numbers of the date (11/23) to honour the sequence. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.

images.title: Shelter among the waves
images.caption: The chapel and hermitage of Santa Justa in Cantabria, Spain
images.desc: Tucked into the cliffs of northern Spain's rugged coastline, the 16th-century Hermitage of Santa Justa, seen in today's image, overlooks the crashing waves of the Cantabrian Sea. Built partly into the rock and associated with relics of Saints Justa and Rufina, the small chapel eventually became a pilgrimage site, its sheltered stone walls creating a remarkable contrast with the powerful waves and rocky cliffs surrounding it.

images.title: Terracotta dreams
images.caption: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
images.desc: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

images.title: Feasting in the fjords
images.caption: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway
images.desc: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, Northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit this region during the winter months, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are famous for bubble-net feeding, a remarkable hunting technique in which whales blow rings of bubbles to corral fish before lunging upwards, open-mouthed, to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquillity in Norway's wild north.

images.title: Where ideas take shape
images.caption: World Philosophy Day
images.desc: It's World Philosophy Day, when big thinkers gather to discuss life's eternal mysteries. To celebrate, today's image features the 'Body of Knowledge' sculpture at Goethe University in Frankfurt, Germany, which moulds steel letters from eight different alphabets into a human form. Spanish artist Jaume Plensa explains: 'Our body is the home of the spirit. The place in which ideas live.' On World Philosophy Day, we're all encouraged to look beyond easy answers and explore the questions that shape us, and the world around us.
